# AF 第一章 原文基线（清理对齐版 v0.1）

## Chapter One

[P01] Mr. Jones, of the Manor Farm, locked the hen-houses for the night. But he was too drunk to remember the pop-holes. His lantern light danced as he lurched（踉跄着走） across the yard. At the back door he kicked off his boots, took a last glass of beer from the barrel（桶）, and went up to bed. Mrs. Jones was already snoring.

[P02] As soon as the bedroom light went out, there was a stirring（搅动） all through the farm buildings. Word had gone round that old Major, the prize Middle White boar（公猪）, had had a strange dream and wanted to tell the other animals about it. They had agreed to meet in the big barn（谷仓） as soon as Mr. Jones was safely out of the way. Old Major, whose show name was Willingdon Beauty, was so well regarded on the farm that everyone was ready to lose an hour's sleep to hear what he had to say.

[P03] At one end of the big barn, on a raised platform（舞台）, Major was settled on his straw（稻草） bed, under a lantern. He was twelve years old and quite fat, but still a majestic（威严的） pig, with a wise and kind look. Presently, as the other animals arrived, he lay down on his side.

[P04] First came the three dogs, Bluebell, Jessie, and Pincher. Then came the pigs, who sat down in the straw in front of the platform. The hens sat on the window-sills. The pigeons flew up to the rafters（椽子）. The sheep and cows lay down behind the pigs and began to chew（咀嚼）. The two cart-horses, Boxer and Clover, came in together. They walked very slowly and put down their big hoof（蹄） with great care, not wanting to step on any small animal in the straw. Clover was a stout（肥胖的） motherly mare（母马） near middle life, who had never got her shape back after her fourth foal（马驹）. Boxer was huge, not very clever, but all the animals respected him for his steady（平稳） character and tremendous（极大的） power to work. After the horses came Muriel, the white goat, and Benjamin, the donkey. Benjamin was the oldest animal on the farm, and the worst tempered. He seldom talked, and when he did, he usually made some cynical（冷嘲的） remark（评论）. Last of all came the cat, who looked round for the warmest place.

[P05] When all the animals had come together, Major began: "Now, comrades（同志们）, what is this life of ours like? Let us face it: our lives are miserable, full of hard work, and short. We are born, we get just enough food to keep us breathing, and those who can work are forced to work until they use up all their strength... No animal in England knows what happiness or rest means after he is one year old. No animal in England is free. The life of an animal is pain and slavery（奴役）: that is the plain truth."

[P06] "But is this just how nature works? Is it because our land is too poor to give a good life to those who live on it? No, comrades, a thousand times no! The soil of England is rich... it could feed many more than the animals living there now. Our farm could feed a dozen horses... it grows enough food for five. So why do we stay in this miserable（悲惨的） life? Because almost all the food we make is stolen from us by human beings. There, comrades, is the answer to all our problems. It is put in one word—Man. Man is the only creature（生物） that eats without producing. He does not give milk, he does not lay eggs, he is too weak to pull the plough, he cannot run fast enough to catch rabbits. Yet he is master of all the animals. He makes them work, he gives back only the least they need to keep from starving（挨饿）, and the rest he keeps for himself. Our work turns the soil, our dung（粪便） makes it rich, and yet not one of us owns more than his bare（仅够） skin（皮肤）. You cows... how many thousands of gallons（加仑） of milk have you given this year? And what happened to that milk?... And the hens... how many eggs?... And you, Clover, where are those four foals（小马） you had?... In the end, no animal escapes the cruel knife."

[P07] "That is the answer to all our problems. It is one word—Man. Take Man away, and the true cause of hunger and too much work is gone for ever."

[P08] "And remember, comrades, your resolution... I do not know when that Rebellion（造反） will come, in a week or in a hundred years... but I know, as surely as I see this straw under my feet, that late（迟早） justice will be done. Fix your eyes on that, comrades... And among us animals let there be perfect unity（团结）, perfect comradeship（友谊） in the struggle（斗争）. All men are enemies. All animals are comrades."

[P09] "Whatever goes upon two legs is an enemy. Whatever goes upon four legs, or has wings, is a friend. And remember also that in fighting against Man, we must not come to resemble（相似） him. Even when you have beaten him, do not copy his bad ways. No animal must ever live in a house, or sleep in a bed, or wear clothes, or drink alcohol（酒精）, or smoke tobacco（烟草）, or touch money, or trade. All the habits of Man are evil. And, above all, no animal must ever be a tyrant（暴君） over his own kind... All animals are equal."

[P10] "And now, comrades, I will tell you about my dream last night... it was a dream of the earth as it will be when Man is gone... I cannot describe it to you. It was a dream of something long past... But I have little time left... I must pass it on to you."

[P11] Major says that when he was young, his mother and other sows（母猪） sang an old tune, Beasts（野兽） of England. He knows only the tune and three words... "It is time that I passed it on to you."

[P12] Old Major cleared his throat and began to sing: "Beasts（野兽） of England, beasts（野兽） of Ireland, beasts of every land and clime（地方）, hearken（倾听） to my joyful tidings（消息） of the golden future time." The animals sang it too, five times, and in the excitement, seven times.

[P13] The song woke the farm: cows lowed, dogs barked, and Jones woke. All was in an uproar.

[P14] Jones grabbed（抓住） his gun and fired number 6 shot into the dark. The pellets（颗粒） hit the barn wall and the meeting ended fast. Everyone ran to his own sleeping-place. The birds jumped on to their perches, the animals lay down, and the whole farm was asleep in a moment.
